id: RF-10 (watch report picks its file name by exclusive create)
note: `watch report` with no --out writes <watch>/reports/<date>_watch-report.md, else the next free -2, -3 ... name. It picked the name by a check, then wrote: two runs on the same date could pick one name, and the second read the clash as `REFUSED: output folder not writable` (exit 73). The name is now taken by an exclusive create and a clash moves on to the next number: 12 runs at once each write their own file, and a name taken by a dangling link (which a check reads as free) is skipped, never written through or replaced. A file that is already there where --out points (watch report), or a report zip whose name is taken (two runs in one second), is no folder problem: it prints `REFUSED: output file exists`, still exit 73, and the file is left as it was. The steps that plant a link need real symlinks (Git for Windows' MSYS perl makes none: sitting 4, T1); the clash with another run's file needs none, and the steps after the links do not count on them.

steps.name: a first report takes the plain name
a name another run took is skipped, its file left as it was
12 reports at once: each writes its own file
a name taken by a dangling link is skipped
watch report --out at a file that exists: output file exists, the file kept
watch report --out at a dangling link: output file exists, nothing written through it
a first report zip into a folder
a second one in the same second: the zip name clashes, output file exists
--out at a folder that is missing: still output folder not writable
